purpose: The by-PNU panel Gold tables (and the unit price history, root ADR-0190) the scheduled job foundation-gold-panel-rebuild.service rebuilds (orchestration/jobs.v1.json gold_panel_rebuild), in the order it rebuilds them, with each table's producer, the producer flags the job passes, the Spark size it runs at, and how many rows a rebuild may lose against the current snapshot before it is refused. The Silver inputs are the producer's own constants (root ADR-0130), not listed here. infra/lakehouse/spark/jobs/gold_rebuild.py reads this file; scripts/ops/gold-panel-rebuild.sh reads the spark sizes. `incremental` (root ADR-0180) lets a rebuild recompute only the PNUs whose inputs changed and merge them, up to max_changed_key_fraction of the Gold, after a parity sample of parity_sample_keys unchanged PNUs agrees; past it, the rebuild is full. Every table declares `incremental` or a `full_reason` saying why it rebuilds whole (a kind under `kind_tables.overrides.<lane>.full_reason`), or gold_rebuild.load_contract refuses the contract (root ADR-0312). A producer's optional input (the parcel lineage) that does not exist or holds no rows refuses the plan, unless the table names it under `absent_inputs_accepted` with its reason; that entry is refused once the input exists.

gold.parcel_panel.max_row_loss_reason: One row per current parcel. A monthly national parcel refresh moves the count by far less than 1% (parcels split, merge or retire a few thousand at a time out of about 40 million); losing more means an input lost a region or a join broke, which must not reach the bake.

unmeasured_inputs.silver.parcel_lineage: Absent from the catalog when the parcel rebuild was measured (2026-10-03) and still absent on 2026-10-04, so the 20g cap was shown only with --no-carry-lineage, where the run already peaked at 18.0GiB anon. Carrying the lineage adds a join; measure it before a run may read it (root ADR-0139).

incremental.reason: Root ADR-0180. Past 30% of the 39.9M PNUs recomputing them costs most of a full rebuild and the copy-on-write merge still copies the untouched rows of every file it touches, so the full rebuild is the cheaper commit. 20,000 unchanged PNUs (0.05%) rebuilt beside the changed ones prove the current Gold is what the build makes of its pins; they ride the same input scan.

gold.building_panel.max_row_loss_reason: One row per PNU that has a building title or unit. Building registers grow; a monthly refresh moves the count by far less than 1% of about 6 million. Losing more means an input lost a region or a join broke, which must not reach the bake.

incremental.reason: Root ADR-0180. Past 30% of the 5.95M PNUs recomputing them costs most of a full rebuild and the copy-on-write merge still copies the untouched rows of every file it touches, so the full rebuild is the cheaper commit. 20,000 unchanged PNUs (0.3%) rebuilt beside the changed ones prove the current Gold is what the build makes of its pins; they ride the same input scan.

gold.unit_price.max_row_loss_reason: One row per PNU with a priced unit (root ADR-0190). A price vintage keeps every reference date it ever published and units are rarely removed, so a monthly refresh moves the count by far less than 1%; losing more means a vintage lost a region or the unit join broke, which must not reach the bake.

incremental.reason: Root ADR-0180, as for the building panel. A monthly vintage changes the prices of few units, so its PNUs are recomputed and merged; a new reference date a year changes most priced PNUs and runs the full rebuild, which is then the cheaper commit.

gold.unit_price.max_price_history_shrink_reason: A price vintage keeps every reference date it ever published (root ADR-0185), so a unit's price history only grows; a unit loses records only when its register is retired, a few at a time. On 2026-10-11 a vintage loaded in part made a Gold in which 47,153 units had lost about 65% of their records (not served only because that day's bake failed). The producer refuses, before it writes, a Gold in which more than 0.1% of the current Gold's units keep fewer records or none.

pins_from.reason: Root ADR-0190. A unit's price is served under the PNU its building document carries it, so both documents must place each unit from the same register snapshots: a unit relinked to another title between two separate pins would be under one PNU in the building document and another in the price document. The rebuild pins these inputs to the snapshots the current building Gold was built from (it runs after the building panel in `all`), never to their heads.

code_version.purpose: Every producer commit records its code version (infra/lakehouse/spark/jobs/gold_code_version.py: the producer script, the modules of spark/jobs it imports transitively, and the JSON contracts they name) beside its source pins; the planner rebuilds a table in full when that version changes. A module named here cannot change a Gold row, so it and what only it imports are left out of the version, and a change to it rebuilds nothing.

plumbing_modules.gold_rebuild: The planner and the commit writer: it decides whether to rebuild and writes the producer's frame unchanged with summary entries.
plumbing_modules.gold_fingerprint: Computes the summary fingerprint of rows already built; it does not build them.
plumbing_modules.section_coverage: A check that refuses a build before it writes; it never alters a row.
plumbing_modules.lakehouse_engine: Spark session, catalog and R2 retry settings: how the rows are read and written, not which. The session time zone (UTC) is set by each producer.
plumbing_modules.lakehouse_snapshot_pins: Parses the pins file; which snapshot is read is the recorded source pin itself.

industrial_complex_lakehouse_contracts.j.reason: Every lakehouse table's contract in one file: 39 of its commits in the 30 days to 2026-10-28, most for tables no panel reads (court auction, place id, boundaries). A table's rows follow its own contract and its inputs' (their columns, keys and current-row rule), and the shared value domains.

r2-connections.contract.json.reason: Every R2 connection and serving setting in one file: 38 of its commits in the same 30 days, 16 for section packs and 12 for the building gateway that no Gold producer reads. A producer reads its by-PNU lanes (kind lines and their columns) and the building gateway's PNU pattern.

section_coverage.purpose: Every table that carries served sections (the host panel of a kind line in config/r2-connections.contract.json by_pnu_lanes, and each kind table) is held to this one bound before it writes (infra/lakehouse/spark/jobs/section_coverage.py). Per section and per 시도 (the PNU's first two digits), and over the whole table, a panel's share of PNUs whose section is non-empty, or a kind table's count of them, may fall by at most max_share_drop_fraction of what the served snapshot (the plan's previous Gold head) has. A 시도 whose served count is below min_region_pnus is judged only inside the whole table. 시도 codes a pair in reference.legal_dong_code_change joins, split between the served snapshot and the build, are compared as one region.
section_coverage.reason: Measured 2026-10-17 on gold.parcel_panel (Trino, read-only): between the served snapshots of 10-14 and today no section of any 시도 fell by more than 1.3% (land rights of 시도 28; the transfer history of 시도 41 grew 11% as the 10-14 build had missed it). The 10-16 morning snapshot, rows unchanged at 39,861,511, had the forest ledger, transfer history and land rights of 시도 29 and 46 at 0 and lost 21-22% of 시도 28's forest ledger and land rights; 5% leaves four times the measured drift and refuses every one of those. Below 1,000 PNUs (land rights of 시도 36: 865) one refresh can move a share by more than 5%, so such a 시도 counts only in the whole table.

kind_tables.purpose: The rebuild of every by-PNU data kind (a config/r2-connections.contract.json by_pnu_lanes line that names a host, infra/lakehouse/spark/jobs/by_pnu_kinds.py). gold_rebuild.load_contract adds one table per kind line after the tables above, in the contract's lane order: gold.<lane with - as _>, unit <lane>, this producer run with --lane <lane>, these bounds, and every input pinned to the host panel's current Gold with a parity check against it. A kind is therefore rebuilt, checked and baked from its line alone.
kind_tables.max_row_loss_reason: One row per PNU that has the kind's section, a subset of its host panel's rows. A monthly vintage moves those PNUs by far less than 1%; losing more means an input lost a region or a join broke, which must not reach the bake.

parcel-public-auction.max_row_loss_reason: The 공매 kind's rows are the parcels with an OPEN Onbid auction as of the build (root ADR-0287 §7), which open and close every day — unlike the slowly-growing registers the 1% default is for, this count swings widely day to day (a batch of rounds closing drops those PNUs). The bound here catches a catastrophic loss (an input lost a region, a join broke, or, as on 2026-10-21, a producer change that drops real sales) rather than normal daily variation; tighten it once the daily open-auction volatility is measured against a clean baseline.

incremental.reason: Root ADR-0180, as for the host panels. A vintage reaches the PNUs its rows name; an input the host panel reads whole (its WHOLE_TABLE_INPUTS) rebuilds the kinds that read it whole.

pins_from_host_panel.reason: Root ADR-0193 §3 and §6-2. While the host panel is what the web reads, a kind is that panel's section: every input is pinned to the snapshots the current panel was built from, so a PNU is never alive in one lane and retired in another, and every full rebuild checks the kind against the panel on every PNU before it writes. The kinds run after the tables above, so a kind's first build (a full one) cannot hold the panels past the job's timeout. When a host panel retires, this pin goes with it.
